title: Correcting an element by the radical quotient to make a single generated submodule a free direct summand
author: The Stacks Project Authors
work: Stacks Project, chapter more-algebra.tex (More on Algebra)
source_version: Stacks Project source tree, file more-algebra.tex, corpus local snapshot 20261012
difficulty_reason: The statement produces, for a projective module with infinite rank localizations over a ring whose quotient by its Jacobson radical is Noetherian, an element m in a prescribed submodule M such that the submodule generated by s + m is a free direct summand, given that s and M already generate the whole module (statement lines 39025-39033). The proof has three stages: a reduction modulo the Jacobson radical where projectivity lifts the splitting and the unit criterion applies, a Noetherian stage where finitely many functionals define a vanishing locus, and an iteration argument in which any locus containing a closed point is strictly decreased because a suitable image in the fibre has infinite dimension while the relevant Tor group is finite (proof lines 39035-39104). The infinite dimension claim is the technical heart, since it is what supplies the element independent of the image of the corrected element. The counted span refers three times to results of another chapter, all carried as navigation stubs.
